history_pageLead: A fisherman, an alley, a white boi with a green star on its forehead. How Mangangá went from the street forrós of Coaban to the festival arena.
history_founderP1: Since 1992 Boi Bumbá Mangangá has stood for the pride and tradition of the Coaban neighbourhood, the Javarizinho. It was founded by fisherman Raimundo Dimas, of northeastern Brazilian origin, was born on alley 50 and won the heart of all Benjamin Constant.
history_founderP2: Boi Besouro, the floodplain boi, is white with a green star on its forehead, a symbol of the strength and resilience of the fishermen and farmers who face the Javarizinho floods every year.
history_founderP3: What began as fun in the street forrós gained recognition and made Mangangá the top champion of the Benjamin Constant Folk Festival, with titles won over more than three decades.
items_pageLead: Each item is scored by the jury on festival nights. Meet the roles that bring Mangangá to life in the arena.
items_note: The cast for each item is announced by the board every season. Want to perform an item? Reach us through the membership page.

festival_aboutP1: For more than thirty years, every July Benjamin Constant becomes the cultural capital of the Upper Solimões and welcomes thousands of visitors from the whole region.
festival_aboutP2: The party crosses borders: people come from Islandia in Peru, from Leticia in Colombia, and locals who live far away come home to see the boi. Floats, legends and Amazonian figures fill the bumbódromo arena.
festival_howLead: The jury scores each boi item by item, in three groups. The sum of the nightly scores decides who takes the title.
festival_arriveLead: Benjamin Constant sits where the Javari meets the Solimões, next to Tabatinga, Leticia and Islandia. Pick your route.

visit_pageLead: How to reach the triple border, what to bring and what to do between festival nights.
visit_tipsLead: Three things that make the trip easier for those coming from afar or crossing the border.
visit_tipDocsText: Many people from three countries move across the border. Bring photo ID, and a passport or national ID if coming from Peru or Colombia.
visit_tipMoneyText: Shops take reais and, near the border, also soles and pesos. Pix is accepted almost everywhere, but bring some cash.
visit_tipWeatherText: July is hot and humid, with showers. Light clothes, sunscreen, insect repellent and a rain cover in your bag.
visit_ctaText: Check the festival night dates and arrive in time to wear the green crowd shirt.
